chapter: The 1940s: small groups, Teddy Wilson and Ethel Waters
title: Will Vodery's attempt to launch a group; drafted
summary: Will Vodery admired Babe's voice and Joe's trumpet and backed a group that played college dates until the draft for World War II interrupted.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Then after Benny that's when you decided to try to form a little group of your own. You run right into the '40s then, right? When we got married.
Yeah, but before that we tried to start a group because Mr. Vadery, Will Vadery.
Well, during that time Mr. Vadery ...
I mean a year earlier, I'm sorry.

Yeah, well, he loved Babe's voice and he was trying to set up some things, you know. So, we were introduced and he heard my trumpet playing and he liked my trumpet playing so we got something to go. He knew the people to talk to. So we tried. He had a couple of dollars so we tried.
Well, what we did, we did some things. We did some individual things. We did some, let me see ...
Had some college dates during that time.
And then by the time you really got started, if I'm not interrupting, that we thought we were getting things started, why Uncle Sam sent for Joe for World War II.
... because that stopped that incident right then.
